_: The pinned corresponding-source manifest (LIC-2). It answers two different
questions and the distinction matters:
1. WHAT source corresponds to the binaries we ship? -> `version` plus the
immutable upstream identity of each artefact (a PyPI sha256, a Ubuntu
pool file, a git commit). These are recorded here and must never be
edited without re-deriving them from upstream.
2. IS a published bundle the one we claim? -> `sha256` of each artefact
as fetched, recorded by `scripts/fetch-corresponding-source.py --record`
and committed. Anyone can re-fetch and compare.
`version` is CHECKED AGAINST THE INSTALLED ENVIRONMENT by
scripts/check-licences.py on every `just lint` and every CI run, using
`detect` below. A wheel bump that moves OCCT is therefore loud: the gate
fails naming the old and new versions, and this file has to be re-pinned
before anything can be published. docs/LICENSING.md §7.

bundle.attach_to: the same GitHub release that publishes the container images
bundle.why: LGPL-2.1 §6(d) wants equivalent access to the source from the same place the object code is offered. Pointing at a third party who may retire a URL is the weakest defensible reading; mirroring under our own release is the strong one. docs/LICENSING.md §7.

detect.note: Every OCCT library carries its release in the SONAME tail (libTKernel-<hash>.so.7.9.3). All 46 must agree.

artefacts.commit_source: git rev-parse HEAD of https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT @ V7_9_3, recorded by scripts/fetch-corresponding-source.py

verify_version.note: Checked against the cloned tree's OWN build metadata, not against the tag name. A tag is a label a human typed and can be moved; these constants are what the binaries were compiled from.

artefacts.note: Fetched as a git clone verified by COMMIT, not as the /archive/refs/tags/ tarball: GitHub generates those on demand and their bytes have changed under people before (gzip settings), so a sha256 pinned to one is a gate that fails for the wrong reason. A commit id is immutable. The checked-out tree is then packed deterministically by scripts/fetch-corresponding-source.py (sorted names, zeroed ownership, fixed mtimes, gzip mtime 0), so `sha256` here is reproducible from `commit` alone — verified 2026-08-01 by three independent clone-and-pack runs producing byte-identical archives.
artefacts.measured: https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/archive/refs/tags/V7_9_3.tar.gz is 403 through the Loft dev container's egress proxy, but `git clone --depth 1 --branch V7_9_3` over HTTPS succeeds. The block is on release-asset downloads, not on git. This leg therefore RAN here.

artefacts.sha256_source: PyPI JSON index for planegcs 0.8.0, re-verified by download 2026-08-01 (digest recomputed from the received bytes)
artefacts.note: The PyPI sdist for the exact version whose wheel we install. Verified to contain the PlaneGCS solver itself — src/planegcs/{GCS,Constraints,Geo,SubSystem,qp_eq}.{cpp,h} plus the bindings — and its LGPL-2.1 LICENSE, so it is corresponding source and not merely the Python wrapper. Files under files.pythonhosted.org are immutable. Use this hashed URL, NOT the legacy /packages/source/p/... path: that path returned a ZERO-BYTE body with a success status through this project's egress proxy, which a naive fetch would have bundled as 'the source'.

artefacts.note: Upstream tarball as Ubuntu shipped it.

artefacts.note: The Debian/Ubuntu delta. WITHOUT this the .orig tarball is not the corresponding source of the binary we ship — the binary is built from orig + these patches.
Ubuntu's own source-package description; its Checksums-Sha256 stanza independently attests the two files above, so the bundle carries its own provenance proof.

_: The GCC runtime libraries we redistribute (LIC-4), and the decision about
whether they carry a source duty. They are NOT in `components` above,
because they are not in the mirrored bundle — see `decision`. They are
recorded here anyway, per file, because a decision that rests on WHICH
binaries these are is only auditable if we say which binaries they are.
scripts/check-licences.py reads `files` on every `just lint`, in CI, and
inside the image build: every GPL-with-exception binary in the tree must
match a record here by GNU build-id (or by sha256 when the binary carries
no build-id). A wheel bump that swaps in a runtime from a different GCC
build is therefore LOUD, which is the property the LIC-4 investigation
found missing — the vendored set is a property of somebody else's build
machine and changes without notice.
gcc_runtime.decision: The GCC Runtime Library Exception discharges the duty for the way Loft conveys these binaries. They are not mirrored, and no source offer is made for them.
gcc_runtime.decided: 2026-08-01 (LIC-4). This is the Loft project's reading of the licence, not legal advice.
reasoning: The exception's §1 grants permission 'to propagate a work of Target Code formed by combining the Runtime Library with Independent Modules, even if such propagation would otherwise violate the terms of GPLv3, provided that all Target Code was generated by Eligible Compilation Processes. You may then convey such a combination under terms of your choice'. Conveying object code without corresponding source is precisely what would 'otherwise violate the terms of GPLv3' (§6), so the grant covers it; and 'under terms of your choice' is inconsistent with an inherited §6 duty.

Our image is that combination and nothing else: libgomp/libgfortran/libquadmath are present only because compiled extension modules (OCP, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn) DT_NEEDED them. Those modules are Independent Modules by the exception's §0 definition — they require the Runtime Library for execution but are not based on it.

'Eligible' holds: every one of these modules is built by GCC (or, where a wheel uses clang, by a toolchain that is not a work based on GCC — the second branch of the §0 definition). No non-GPL-compatible optimiser touches a GCC intermediate representation anywhere in this stack.

The narrow thing the exception does NOT plainly cover is conveying a Runtime Library on its own, detached from Target Code — a distro shipping libgomp as an installable package is doing that, which is why distros ship GCC source and we are not being inconsistent with them. Loft never does: these files exist inside the image only as the runtime of the code that links them.
what_would_change_this: Publishing a Runtime Library as an artefact in its own right (a 'gcc runtime' image or package) rather than inside a combined work.
Any part of the stack switching to a toolchain that is a work based on GCC plus a non-GPL-compatible plugin/optimiser — that breaks 'Eligible Compilation Processes' and the grant with it.
A wheel starting to vendor libstdc++ or libgcc_s: same exception, same reasoning, but they must be identified and recorded here rather than assumed.
gcc_runtime.why_the_versions_are_recorded_anyway: So the reading above is checkable rather than asserted, and so a recipient who takes the stricter reading knows exactly which source to ask its distributor for. Recording them cost one afternoon of evidence; the backlog item had assumed it was impossible for the numpy/scipy set, and it was not.

identification.method: GNU build-id, read out of the shipped binary. Two files with the same build-id are the same build of the same source; auditwheel's rename/RPATH patching preserves it. Corroborated per file by the .comment section, by symbol-version nodes, and by the auditwheel CycloneDX SBOM of whichever wheel vendored the file.
identification.auditwheel_naming_rule: auditwheel renames a vendored library to <stem>-<sha256[:8] of the file it copied>.so.<v>. That makes the FILENAME a content-addressed pointer at its own source file, and a doubled tag (libgfortran-<a>-<b>.so.5.0.0) means the file came from another wheel that had already been repaired. Verified here: the scipy_openblas32 wheel's libgfortran-040039e1.so.5.0.0 hashes to 0352e75f…, which is exactly the tail tag of the copy we ship.
identification.auditwheel_sbom_caveat: The '#…' suffix of an SBOM bom-ref is NOT a content digest. Measured 2026-08-01: scipy's SBOM and scipy_openblas32's SBOM carry the IDENTICAL suffix 3362720c… for libgfortran while naming different packages (almalinux libgfortran 8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1 vs centos libgfortran5 8.3.1-2.1.1.el7) and describing demonstrably different binaries. Reading it as a file hash would produce a confident, wrong identification. Use build-id.

files.evidence: Its .comment section says verbatim 'GCC: (conda-forge gcc 15.2.0-19) 15.2.0' — for a GCC runtime library, which is built by the compiler it ships with, that string is the library's own version. Corroborated by its symbol-version nodes reaching GOMP_5.1.3 (GCC 14+), where the el8 libgomp below stops at GOMP_5.0. It carries no build-id (conda-forge strips it), so this record is keyed on sha256. It is absent from the wheel's auditwheel SBOM, which lists only Ubuntu 20.04 dpkg packages — consistent with a conda toolchain rather than the build image's package manager.

corresponding_source.upstream_base: GCC 15.2.0 — https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc, tag releases/gcc-15.2.0, commit 5115c7e447fc07457443df874bf57840e8316d5f (resolved by git ls-remote 2026-08-01)
corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that release plus the conda-forge ctng-compilers feedstock's patch series for build 19

files.arrives_via: scipy 1.18.0 wheel (auditwheel took it from the manylinux_2_28 build image)
files.evidence: scipy's own auditwheel SBOM names pkg:rpm/almalinux/libgfortran@8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1, and this is the file it can be describing: auditwheel only records packages it resolved through the build image's rpm database, the OTHER libgfortran in scipy.libs came from a wheel (doubled hash tag), and this one needs GLIBC_2.27 symbols that el7's glibc 2.17 does not have. scipy_openblas64's SBOM independently names the same rpm.

corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM — upstream GCC 8.5.0 plus Red Hat's and AlmaLinux's patch series. The upstream tarball ALONE would not correspond, exactly as LibRaw's .orig alone does not (docs/LICENSING.md §7.1).
corresponding_source.url_not_recorded_because: every AlmaLinux/CentOS/Rocky/kernel.org/gnu.org host is policy-denied from this project's dev container (measured 2026-08-01: CONNECT tunnel 403 on nine hosts, git and raw.githubusercontent excepted). We do not record a URL we have not fetched.

files.evidence: scipy's auditwheel SBOM names pkg:rpm/almalinux/libquadmath@8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1; same reasoning as the libgfortran above. Corroborated by its QUADMATH_1.0 + QUADMATH_1.1 version nodes, where the el7 libquadmath below (GCC 4.8.5) has QUADMATH_1.0 only.

corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM (upstream GCC 8.5.0 plus the distro patch series)
corresponding_source.url_not_recorded_because: see the libgfortran record above — the hosts are policy-denied here and we do not record unfetched URLs.

files.arrives_via: numpy 2.5.1 wheel (numpy ships NO auditwheel SBOM)
files.evidence: Identified by transfer, which is the whole reason build-id is the key: numpy records nothing, but this file's build-id is byte-identical to scipy's SBOM-identified libgfortran, and its .text/.rodata/.data.rel.ro sections hash identically to it. Same build, therefore same source. Its inner hash tag 83c28eba is the same content-addressed pointer scipy's copy carries, i.e. both build images had a byte-identical /usr/lib64/libgfortran.so.5.0.0.

corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM (upstream GCC 8.5.0 plus the distro patch series)

files.evidence: Build-id identical to scipy's SBOM-identified libquadmath, and .text/.rodata byte-identical to it. Same build, same source.

corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM (upstream GCC 8.5.0 plus the distro patch series)

files.evidence: scikit-learn's auditwheel SBOM names pkg:rpm/almalinux/libgomp@8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1, and it is the only libgomp in that wheel. Corroborated by the annobin notes left in the binary: 'running gcc 8.5.0 20210514', the el8 GCC build date.

corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM (upstream GCC 8.5.0 plus the distro patch series)

files.arrives_via: scipy 1.18.0 wheel, which re-vendored it from the scipy-openblas32 wheel (doubled hash tag)
files.evidence: Traced one wheel further up and then verified by download: scipy_openblas32's auditwheel SBOM names pkg:rpm/centos/libgfortran5@8.3.1-2.1.1.el7, and the libgfortran-040039e1.so.5.0.0 inside that wheel has this exact build-id with byte-identical .text/.rodata/.data.rel.ro. Downloaded 2026-08-01 from files.pythonhosted.org: scipy_openblas32 0.3.31.188.0 wheel sha256 29534062c634a635c4d86b7f238541a81a39e457048ad3d717f54843530a0112; its libgfortran-040039e1.so.5.0.0 is 2723513 bytes, sha256 0352e75f0719d9a299cb52919977eb5d7bd249d1fcad06d5e14030b272aae619 — whose first 8 hex are the tail tag of the file we ship. Versions 0.3.31.126.5 and 0.3.31.159.0 carry the identical file. Independently corroborated: this binary needs no glibc symbol above GLIBC_2.17 (el7), where the el8 libgfortran above needs GLIBC_2.27.

corresponding_source.distro_source_package: CentOS 7 source rpm for libgfortran5 8.3.1-2.1.1.el7 (the SBOM records the binary package, not the source package name)
corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM only. There is NO upstream release to fall back on: FSF released 8.3.0, 8.4.0 and 8.5.0 and never an 8.3.1 (checked against the tags of https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc, 2026-08-01) — 8.3.1 is a distributor snapshot. This is the clearest case in the set that mirroring an upstream tarball would have been a confident guess rather than corresponding source.
corresponding_source.url_not_recorded_because: vault.centos.org and every other distro host are policy-denied here (measured).

files.arrives_via: scipy 1.18.0 wheel, re-vendored from the scipy-openblas32 wheel
files.evidence: Same chain as the libgfortran above: scipy_openblas32's SBOM names pkg:rpm/centos/libquadmath@4.8.5-44.el7, and that wheel's libquadmath-96973f99.so.0.0.0 (247609 bytes, sha256 934c22ded0e7d169c4d4678876c96051adf3d94545da962f60b41659b075da3b) has this build-id and byte-identical .text. The version looks wrong beside a GCC 8.3.1 libgfortran and is not: on CentOS 7 the Fortran runtime came from a devtoolset while libquadmath stayed at the base system's GCC 4.8.5. Corroborated by its symbol versions — QUADMATH_1.0 only, no QUADMATH_1.1.

corresponding_source.complete_source_is: that SRPM (upstream GCC 4.8.5, https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc tag releases/gcc-4.8.5 commit 2da13f5a051c8a28a85311fea990355b4797c179, plus the distro patch series)

gcc_runtime.source_access: Nothing is mirrored for these, by decision. If a recipient asks anyway, the honest answer is above: for seven of the eight files the corresponding source is a distro SRPM, named here exactly, which that distro publishes; for the eighth it is GCC 15.2.0 plus conda-forge's patch series. Loft will help a requester locate them (open an issue), but does not claim to have mirrored source it has not fetched.

no_source_obligation.why: Pure Python. MPL-2.0 §3.2 wants the Source Code Form available to recipients of the Executable Form; for certifi the image already contains the .py files themselves, so the obligation is discharged by the artifact.
Dual-licensed; Loft elects the permissive arm (FIPL-1.0, FTL). Those arms carry no source-provision duty. Versions are on the record in docs/LICENSING.md §7 anyway.

SETTLED 2026-08-01 (LIC-4): the GCC Runtime Library Exception's §1 permits propagating the Runtime Library combined with Independent Modules 'under terms of your choice', and that combination is the only form in which Loft ever conveys them. Full reasoning, and the exact GCC build behind each of the eight files — all eight identified, none guessed — are in the `gcc_runtime` block above.
